digitalcore._rules_read: 2026-08-21, from the site's own Rules page and FAQ
digitalcore._min_ratio_note: Below it: five days of ratio watch, then leeching is revoked. The account stays enabled, so this costs downloads rather than the account.
digitalcore._hit_and_run_note: Their real rule, from the FAQ: the obligation starts once 10% of a torrent is downloaded, and clears at 5 days of seeding OR ratio 1:1. Freeleech is NOT exempt. A torrent that stops announcing for one hour is listed as a hit and run immediately, with 10 days to fix it before it becomes permanent and needs points, upload credit or a donation to remove. Five of them is a warning, more is a download ban. **The site is the only source of truth for seed time**: it counts only what it saw announced, so the client's own counter means nothing here.
digitalcore.cross_seed: explicitly allowed by rule 2, in those words
digitalcore.never: add trackers to their .torrent files, or enable DHT/PEX on them: rule 2 forbids modifying their torrents at all, which is exactly what fixed TorrentLeech's passkey
digitalcore._banned_clients_note: qBittorrent is not on the list, so this box is fine.

leech_bonus.scarcity_factor: 1 + (1 / seeders), so a torrent with a single seeder pays double

digitalcore._leech_bonus_note: The single most valuable mechanic on any tracker here: every 10 GB actively seeded is 1% off what a download costs against ratio, averaged over 7 days, and 1 TB seeded is 100%, which is a site-wide freeleech. Only 50 GiB per torrent counts, so many medium torrents beat a few huge ones. Currently at 12% with about 272 GB seeded.
free_when: new torrents, for 24 h after upload, if the download completes inside the window
digitalcore._proxy_note: The website is hosted in Russia, where VPN IPs are blocked, so the site and IRC may be unreachable from behind one. That is what trackerprxy.digitalcore.club is, and why one cross-seed announces there.

irc.points: +0.4p per hour idling in #digitalcore, and the site username must match

digitalcore.api_limits: A normal API key reaches only /api/v1/torrents, /torrents/download/{id} and /torrents/upload. Profile data is blocked, which is why the account cannot be read automatically.
digitalcore._bonus_hold_decision: Measured and rejected on 2026-08-21. Holding this tracker's finished torrents bought 27% of leech bonus, but only 9% of that was free: 94 GB already shares its inodes with the library and costs nothing, while the other 18% was bought with 179 GB of separate copies (RAR archive sets and films already watched). Paying 179 GB for cheaper downloads on a tracker already at ratio 4.21 with 86 GB of headroom solves a problem that does not exist, while the disk it takes is exactly what the TorrentLeech freeleech grabber needs. So the bonus is grown only through hardlinks from now on: the library copies, which seed for free anyway, and cross-seeds, which are hardlinks by construction. `bonus_hold` stays implemented in scripts/trackers/control.py for the day this tracker is leeched from heavily, and stays unconfigured until then.

retrotoon._rules_read: 2026-08-21, from the site's own Rules page
retrotoon._min_ratio_note: No ratio requirement stated. The rule here is seed time, not ratio.
retrotoon._hit_and_run_note: 72 h of seeding, reached within the first 10 days after the download, and the site calls it its strictest rule with no exceptions. The generic 240 h goal in seed-rules.json already exceeds it, so nothing is at risk while no override exists.
retrotoon._tracker_hosts_note: Read on 2026-08-21 out of a real .torrent fetched through Prowlarr, since the host is not in the definition.

btschool._rules_read: 2026-08-21, from the site's own Rules page
btschool._min_ratio_note: The rules say a low ratio costs download privileges but put the number in their FAQ, which has not been read yet.
btschool._hit_and_run_note: 20 h of seeding within 10 days of finishing, regardless of torrent size, and upload above download clears it outright. Ten unmet obligations is a ban, clearing one costs 20000 bonus points, and an H&R ban is lifted only by a 100 CNY donation.
btschool._tracker_hosts_note: Still unknown: the site refuses to serve a .torrent at all (Prowlarr gets 'Invalid torrent file contents'), which is consistent with an account still inside its newbie assessment. Searching works, downloading does not.
btschool._max_upload_note: Their cap, not ours: over 25 MB/s on a reported announce is penalised at three times the reported upload, and over 100 MB/s is an automatic ban. qBittorrent's upload is unlimited and its global limit cannot be set per tracker, so this only becomes a real constraint once something seeds here. Measured peak so far across all trackers: about 0.5 MB/s.

c411._rules_read: 2026-08-21, from the site's own Ratio & Seedtime wiki page
c411._min_ratio_note: Below 0.8 downloads are blocked until the ratio recovers. The account is not disabled, it just cannot leech.
c411._hit_and_run_note: Their H&R system is DISABLED right now, and the wiki documents the rules for when it comes back: 72 h or ratio 1.0 per torrent, a 24 h grace period, exemptions for a global ratio of 2.0, the first three torrents, anything under 100 MB and anything less than half downloaded. Three active violations block downloads, five strikes is a ban. Measured here as if it were on, because it will be.
c411._credit_note: New accounts get 50 GB of upload credit that counts towards the ratio, so the 52.2 GB the site shows is 2.3 GB really uploaded plus the credit. Any headroom figure from this site is inflated by it and does not grow back.
c411._status_2026_08_21: The site itself is in maintenance: its own homepage answers with a Maintenance page from here, which is why Prowlarr cannot parse the XML. Its API key is set, and the nordvpn proxy tag was removed on request, so search should recover on its own.
